topic: Smart Pointers: std::unique_ptr for Exclusive Ownership
explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr are used to manage dynamic memory with automatic resource management, ensuring exception safety and preventing memory leaks. Unlike raw pointers, std::unique_ptr enforces strict ownership semantics, meaning only one unique_ptr can own a given resource at a time. When the unique_ptr goes out of scope, it automatically deletes the managed object, following the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) principle. This concept is essential for writing safe, efficient, and modern C++ code that manages resources without manual delete calls.

example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage the lifetime of a dynamically allocated ClassA object. It shows how to create a unique_ptr with std::make_unique, transfer ownership using std::move, and rely on automatic destruction when the unique_ptr goes out of scope. The code enforces exclusive ownership semantics, preventing multiple pointers from owning the same object, which aligns with modern C++ best practices for resource management.
